title: First tour, personnel and the 1938-39 band
summary: Budd names Robert Crowder, Franz Jackson and the arrangement 'Yellow Five', and calls this one of Hines's best bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: See. So we rented this bus and we went out on our first tour, and I'll tell you the band was very, very, very, very good. We had a real good time. Old Robert Crowder was in the band, Cecil Lewin Irving's nephew.
And we also had Franz Francis-Jackson in the band later on.
Franz Jackson (Inaudible) on the tenor saxophone.
Played clarinet, bassoon, everything. He's got a great Dixieland Band I understand now in Chicago.
He was a pretty good arranger too wasn't he?
Very, very good arranger. In fact he started to make some beautiful things in the band. One of his best arrangements that I think we recorded was called 'Yellow Five.'

Yeah. We recorded that in California in 1940. But any way, all of this happened in the latter part of '38, 1938, and we went along with that band through '39. Now, I actually believe this was one of Earl's world's best bands. Because the cats were a little bit more modern, I mean, you know the intonation in the band was better, we were a little more conscious of playing together. And then by me being the straw boss handling the rehearsals, I was very sensitive about playing together, tuning up.
